newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FOCUS-Anglo backs down under EU pressure.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Anglo backs down under EU pressure.

text.p: South Africa's Anglo American Corp, under pressure from the European Commission, has backed down and agreed to cut its stake in Lonrho Plc to under 10 percent, sources close to Anglo said on Friday.
The sources said Anglo will settle its dispute with the Commission over its 25.8 percent stake in Lonrho by reducing the stake over two years.

The EU has said Anglo's stake in Lonrho -- which has substantial interest in two South African platinum mines -- would put control of the world's platinum industry in the hands of Anglo and another South African mining house, Gencor Ltd .
The Commission said in a Statement of Objections in February that Anglo's shareholding in Lonrho had the possibility of the South African conglomerate exercising decisive influence over Lonrho.
The sources said the Commission felt that "platinum was a highly sensitive matter" and such harsh measures were necessary for policy reasons.

"After much deliberation, Anglo American Corp took the view that a settlement of this nature was better than the uncertainty of a battle and agreed with great reluctance to accept the Commission's proposals," one source close to Anglo said.
The settlement would see the remainder of Anglo's stake, around 17 percent, placed in a voting trust to be sold off under supervision of the Commission.
"It is up to the Commission to decide who the list of disqualified buyers are," one source said.
But the Commission's harsh stance and insistance on a stake of less than 10 percent could impact on more aspects of European competition policy and affect other multinational companies.
"This may well have very broad ramifications," one source said.
"Their policy is that they want to emasculate the shareholder and their magical barrier is 10 percent," said another source.

Analysts have said that Anglo's main aim in buying the 18 percent stake in Lonrho of the company's former chief executive Dieter Bock, was to gain Lonrho's 33.6 percent stake in Ashanti Goldfields Company Ltd AGC.GH.
The sources said the settlement would not impact on any future Anglo plans to pursue Lonrho's other interests in sugar, coal or Ashanti.
"We are still able to pursue what we want to pursue," one source said, adding that there would be no legal barrier put up by the European Union.
"It is not just mining, there are other interests. There's coal (and) there is sugar. There is no legal barrier....the EU is not interested in anything but platinum," one source said.
The sources said Anglo would continue to discuss with Lonrho management their plans and discuss what Anglo "want to achieve".
Anglo was warned against taking control of Lonrho a year ago, when the Commission blocked the proposed merger of Gencor's platinum interests with that of Lonrho.
Anglo American has always contested that its stake gave it control over Lonrho's platinum interests.
Lonrho owns around 73 percent of Eastern and Western Platinum -- its own platinum division -- with 23 percent held by Gencor.
Anglo's platinum division, Anglo American Platinum Corp of South Africa Ltd (Amplats) produces around 38 percent of the world's newly-mined platinum.
Gencor and Lonrho together control 28 percent, according to a Commission statement in April when it blocked the Gencor/Lonrho merger.
